newsitem.title: UK: British city seeks to stop Nazi sale.
newsitem.headline: British city seeks to stop Nazi sale.

text.p: A British city council said on Sunday it wanted to stop a sale of Nazi memorabilia that it feared could attract Nazi sympathisers from Europe and the United States.
Newcastle city council said the auction on August 7 included Nazi-era medals, daggers, swastika flags and even a set of cut-glass items given by Adolf Hitler to SS chief Heinrich Himmler.
Councillor Nigel Dodds of the northeastern city's racial equality committee said: "The last thing that we want to see in Newcastle is the arrival of hundreds of Nazi bargain hunters.
"The ethics of this sale are all wrong and it should be called off. You must be pretty weird anyway to want to spend good money on all this stuff."
Dodds said in a statement he had written to auctioneers Thomas N. Miller asking the firm to reconsider the sale.
The sale would enable some people to make money out of the racially inspired mass murder of millions of other people, Dodds said.
Thomas N. Miller could not be reached for comment.
